title: Swatches
description: Keep the colours you use in the document's own palette, then paint fills and strokes from it with a click.

bubble.title: Swatches: colours you keep
bubble.body: Swatches are the colours you keep. Keep the fill or stroke colour you are using and it stays in this section, saved inside the document itself — it travels with the file.

bubble.title: Watch: a colour ready to keep
bubble.body: The program sets the fill colour to a brick red — the colour you are about to keep.

demo.title: The current fill
demo.body: Setting the fill colour to a brick red — the colour you are about to keep.

demo.title: Keeping it
demo.body: The + Keep fill button in this section saves the current fill colour into the palette below. The demo cannot press panel buttons, so the next step is yours — the red is already set.

bubble.title: Keep the fill colour
bubble.body: Click + Keep fill in the Swatches section. The brick-red fill is added to the palette in this section.

bubble.title: Watch: a different colour
bubble.body: The program changes the fill to blue and draws a rectangle with it, so you can repaint it from the palette.

demo.title: A different colour
demo.body: Fill on, solid blue this time. Drawing a rectangle with I.

demo.title: Blue for now
demo.body: The rectangle lands blue and stays selected. The kept red is waiting in the palette.

bubble.title: Paint the fill from the palette
bubble.body: The blue rectangle is selected. In the Swatches section, click the brick-red swatch you kept — its fill repaints to the kept colour.

bubble.title: Paint the stroke from the palette
bubble.body: Shift+click the same brick-red swatch. Shift sends the colour to the stroke instead — the rectangle's outline turns red.

bubble.title: The whole section
bubble.body: Click a swatch to paint the fill, Shift+click for the stroke, + Keep to save the colour you are using, Alt+click to remove a kept swatch. The eyedropper button samples a colour from any shape on the canvas.
